title: Control operators and control points
blurb: Who must control a station, whose license sets the privileges, and the difference between local, remote and automatic control.

T1E01.why: Every transmission needs a control operator. Even a repeater has one designated, so the answer is **never**.
T1E01.trap: Automatic control doesn't mean no control operator.

T1E02.why: For satellite work, **any amateur allowed on the uplink frequency** can be the control operator. No special rating or membership.

T1E03.why: The **station licensee** designates the control operator, not the FCC or a coordinator.

T1E04.why: Privileges follow whoever is at the mic: the **class of license held by the control operator**.
T1E04.trap: The owner's license or anyone else on the premises doesn't count.

T1E05.why: The control point is **where the control operator function is performed**, not the antenna, transmitter or mailing address.

T1E06.why: A Technician's privileges stop at Technician segments. An Extra's designation, a contest team or a club trustee can't extend them, except in an emergency.

T1E07.why: The **control operator and the licensee** share responsibility for proper operation.
T1E07.trap: Responsibility isn't only one or the other, and bystanders aren't included.

T1E08.why: A repeater runs unattended, which is **automatic control**.
T1E08.trap: Internet operation is remote control. Computer-sent CW or IDs aren't automatic control.

T1E09.why: **Any** station may be remotely controlled, not just repeaters or digital stations.

T1E10.why: Operating a station from elsewhere, such as **over the internet**, is remote control.
T1E10.trap: SDRs, model control and EME are different things.

T1E11.why: A control operator is an amateur **designated by the licensee** to be responsible for transmissions and rule compliance.
T1E11.trap: That's not just whoever is talking, nor the licensee by default.
